title.analysis: Authentic title "WTF Just Happened To The Housing Market?!" is a shock-question frame. The script answers it with a causal sequence (zero rates and QE, pandemic migration, the 2022-23 hiking cycle, rate lock-in, underbuilding, tariffs), so the promise is delivered. The title implies a sudden event; the script describes a multi-year freeze.

script.opening_words: Here's something that should be mathematically impossible. The United States housing market just posted its lowest transaction volume since 1995, meaning fewer homes are selling right now than at any point in 30 years. And in the same breath, home prices are sitting near all-time highs. Simultaneously, fewer people buying, higher prices. In any normal market, those two things cancel each other out. That's how supply and demand works. You learned it in eighth grade, so did I. And yet,
script.ending_words: exactly why it doesn't, that's the first step toward making a decision that actually works for you instead of just participating in collective financial insanity because everyone around you insists that buying is always the right move. Now you do, drop a like if this helped. It genuinely makes a difference. Subscribe if you want to keep running the real math together and I'll see you in the next one.
script.analysis: Full 19584 canonical characters read. A single-narrator housing explainer: paradox hook (lowest sales since 1995 at near-record prices), payment arithmetic, the 2020-21 cheap-money and migration surge, the 2022-23 hiking cycle, affordability gap, rate lock-in, a composite buyer (Maya), the emotional experience and first-time buyer statistics, underbuilding and tariffs, why it is not 2008, rate outlook and lock-in fade, the risk that fast rate cuts raise prices, and decision rules (28-30% of gross, 7-year horizon, rent-and-invest, builder buy-downs). Most payment arithmetic reproduces; the current median price is about $20,000 high, the 46% rise is miscalculated, and several research figures differ from their published sources.

topic.analysis: Why US existing-home sales collapsed while prices stayed near records: rate lock-in, the 2022-23 rate shock, pandemic demand and a decade of underbuilding.
